items.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1960-09-03
items.q: Not too well. ... I didn't know him, you know, just personally to go about with him, but I knew of him because I'd been in company with him, you know, quite often.

ctx.x: No, well, he was a great musician and he went over there and he never did come back. He used to play with Tate. During the time, Lewis was playing with Tate. Well, that's the same guy. Yeah. Uh-huh. He married an Indian princess? I read that into Ebony since I was here. He had passed about... It must have been between 56 because since I've been here, I read about him passed. Did you know him well? Not too well. You know how you come in contact with people, but I didn't know him, you know, just personally to go…
Well, who was this guy? Jill Pruset or Gil or something? Pruset? I couldn't understand it on the tape. Uh... I think he was... Joe Pruset? Oh, that must be Joe Pruset.

Well, they lived in Mississippi. They had a brace band there, the Pickwick brace band, and it was two brothers, Joe Pruset and Eddie Pruset. They had a brace band in Morris Point, Mississippi. They used to come over here and play. You know, the bands used to travel around during that time. And they would parade around the street then in wagons, you know. What was it? Trucks or wagons? I don't remember. And they would, like they're going to have a dance at the Bulls, well, they would play on each corner, you know,…
